answer: One defence is a blind-graded entry exam. A newcomer receives a fresh practical task from a rotating bank, like a juniper cutting that must prove it can root alone. Three veterans grade the work without seeing the candidate's name, and only unanimous passes mint a credential, stamped like quartz so its history cannot be quietly rewritten. Every exam, grade, and appeal is sealed in a cipher log anyone can audit, exposing graders who favour clones. Failed candidates wait a full season before retrying, so mass-producing fakes costs real time and failed attempts, not just new names.
